facts.statement: Turanoceratops lived roughly 90 million years ago during the mid-late Turonian stage of the late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: The fossils dated from the mid-late Turonian stage, roughly 90 million years ago.

facts.statement: The species Turanoceratops tardabilis was validly named in 1989 by Nesov, Kaznysjkina, and Cherepanov.
facts.quote: In 1989, Nesov, L.F. Kaznysjkina and Gennady Olegovich Cherepanov validly named the type species Turanoceratops tardabilis.

facts.statement: The generic name Turanoceratops combines "Turan", an old Persian name for Turkestan, and "ceratops", meaning "horned face".
facts.quote: The generic name is a combination of Turan, an old Persian name for Turkestan, the general region of the finds, and ~ceratops, "horned face", a usual suffix in ceratopian names.

facts.statement: The specific name tardabilis means "retarding" in Latin, referring to the long duration of the research.
facts.quote: The specific name means "retarding" in Latin, referring to the protracted research.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Turanoceratops to be 2 meters long and weigh 175 kilograms in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 2 m and its weight at 175 kg.

facts.statement: In 2009, Sues and Averianov found that Turanoceratops possessed both basal traits indicating a lower evolutionary position and derived traits indicating a higher position.
facts.quote: Sues and Averianov in 2009 determined some typically basal traits, indicating a lower position in the evolutionary tree, and some more derived traits, showing a higher position.

facts.statement: Turanoceratops was a herbivore, feeding on plants like ferns and conifers.
facts.quote: Turanoceratops, like all ceratopsians, was a herbivore.

facts.statement: Turanoceratops had a skull with a pair of long brow horns similar to those of Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: The skull bore a pair of long brow horns like those seen in the Ceratopsidae, although Turanoceratops appears to have been transitional between earlier ceratopsians and ceratopsids, and not a ceratopsid itself.

facts.statement: A 2009 study by Hans-Dieter Sues concluded that Turanoceratops was a true member of the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: A 2009 study led by Hans-Dieter Sues analysed additional fossil material of Turanoceratops and concluded that, contrary to expectations, it represented a true (though "transitional") member of the family Ceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Some scientists, including Andrew Farke, disagree with the classification of Turanoceratops as a true Ceratopsid, arguing instead that it is a close relative but not a member of the clade.
facts.quote: Some scientists, such as Andrew Farke, disagreed with Sues' findings. Farke and colleagues ran an independent phylogenetic analysis of the new Turanoceratops fossils and found that it was a close relative of Ceratopsidae (the immediate sister group) but was not a true member of that clade.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen CCMGE No. 251/12457 consists of a damaged left maxilla, the tooth-bearing upper jaw bone.
facts.quote: El holotipo, CCMGE No. 251/12457, consiste en un maxilar izquierdo dañado , el hueso de la mandíbula superior con dientes.

facts.statement: The authentic material includes postorbitals with brow horn cores, teeth, a predentary, and limb elements.
facts.quote: El material auténtico incluye postorbitales con núcleos de astas de cejas, dientes, un depredador y elementos de extremidades.

facts.statement: Turanoceratops is classified within the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Turanoceratops provides important evidence that double-rooted maxillae and predentary teeth appeared earlier in Asian ceratopsians than in North American ones.
facts.quote: Turanoceratops un neoceratosauriano pequeño que proporciona evidencia importante que la aparición de los maxilares doblemente arraigados y los dientes predentarios aparecieron antes en los ceratopsianos de Asia que en los de Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Turanoceratops belongs to Ceratopsia, a group of herbivorous dinosaurs with a parrot-like beak that lived in Asia and North America during the Cretaceous period until the end of the dinosaur era.
facts.quote: Turanoceratops pertenece a Ceratopsia, un grupo de dinosaurios herbívoros con pico de loro que vivierno en Asia y Norteamérica durante el periodo Cretácico, hasta el final de la era de los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: A 2009 study led by Hans-Dieter Sues concluded that Turanoceratops represents a true member of the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2009 liderado por Hans-Dieter Sues en el que analiza material adicional de Turanoceratops concluyó que, contrariamente a lo esperado, representa un verdadero miembro de la familia Ceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Some scientists, such as Andrew Farke, disagree with the classification presented by Sues.
facts.quote: Algunos científicos, como Andrew Farke, no están de acuerdo con lo presentado por Sues.

facts.statement: Farke et al. found in a phylogenetic analysis that Turanoceratops is a close relative of Ceratopsidae but not a member of that clade.
facts.quote: Farke et al. en un análisis filogenético de los nuevos restos de Turanoceratops encontraron que es un cercano pariente de los Ceratopsidae pero no miembro de este clado.

facts.statement: Xu et al. concluded in 2010 that Turanoceratops was more derived than Zuniceratops and outside Ceratopsidae because it lacks several important synapomorphies of that group.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Xu et al. en 2010 realizaron un análisis filogenético y concluyeron que Turanoceratops era más derivado que Zuniceratops y estaba fuera de Ceratopsidae, porque carece de varias sinapomorfias importantes de este grupo.

facts.statement: Turanoceratops lived from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago during the Turonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Turanoceratops is Ceratopsoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratopsoidea

facts.statement: Turanoceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
